text:
anya: quick follow-up from last week's cp-separation rfc. can we lock down fallback semantics for when the per-tenant cp-proxy in customer VPC loses connectivity? thinking about graceful failover to regional relay w/ preserved client ips.

nate: +1. main concerns: auth handoff (mTLS), session affinity (kv cache), and per-tenant rate quotas. if we just route to relay, we'll lose original SNAT. need a plan.

ryan: suggestion — keep a short-lived handshake token minted by the agent, presented to relay. relay validates via control-plane signing key. avoids needing peering for auth.

anya: @ryan can you sketch token lifetime and replay protection? also need to maintain prefix cache warming so latency doesn't spike on failover.

ryan: token lifetime idea: 10s nominal, allow <=30s skew for clock drift. each token includes a conn-id nonce for replay protection. relay rejects reused conn-id. sketch: 

```
# example handshake header
X-RD-AGENT-HANDSHAKE: v1 token=eyJ...;conn=abc123;ts=1756004321;sig=MEUCIQ...
```

marta: for kv/prefix cache: agent can stream a compact prefetch manifest to relay on successful handshake (list of top-N prefixes + embedding keys). relay uses that to warm caches, TTL-based.

nate: what about cost? if many tenants fallback simultaneously we'll route a ton of traffic through relay and spike infra cost. need autoscale + burst cap and a circuit-breaker.

oliver: propose fallback policy: probe connectivity for 3s, do 2 local retries with backoff, then failover to relay with header `X-RD-FALLBACK: degraded`. emit metric `cp.fallback.count` and tag reason (health-check|timeout|auth).

anya: agree. also requires operator playbook for rotating signing keys across cp agents and relays. can we use KMS-backed keys per-region and short-lived signing tokens?

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rolling restart of cp-proxy fleet in us-west-2 started at 1756004335.

ryan: implement reconnect/backoff in agent: 200ms -> 1s -> 5s -> 20s, add jitter. if final state is degraded, attempt handshake-as-fallback-only once per minute.

marta: to avoid double-claiming KV cache we should keep per-tenant connection map and use an ownership lease (ttl 30s) persisted to relay on takeover. relay rejects overlapping leases.

nate: also need quota preservation: preserve original request rate windows; relay should consult cp quota service (or cache last-known quotas) to not overserve.

anya: action items: @ryan - draft handshake proto + replay rules, @marta - perf model for cache snapshot size and warming latency, @nate - update cost model and autoscale thresholds + circuit-breaker knobs. oliver - add e2e test in integration harness to simulate CP cutover. i'll own operator playbook draft. sync Thu 10am.

oliver: +1. i'll add a chaos test where 30% of agents flip to relay to validate cost and cache behavior.

anya: thanks all. keeping these semantics consistent across private/dedicated/hosted is key — doc that in the cp ops runbook. :thumbsup:
